thread:
maya: Quick heads-up — linux/gcc13 CI is red after today's toolchain roll. Several link errors when building the static archive for core. Failing job: https://ci.redwood.internal/job/1234 (linux-gcc13-shard-5). Anyone seen this?

CI-bot: build failed for job 1234: exit code 1. Summary: link errors while creating //core:static_lib. Attaching top of link log below.

CI-bot: ```
/usr/bin/ld: bazel-out/k8-fastbuild/bin/core/_objs/foo/bar.o: in function `Foo::Init()':
bar.o:(.text+0x34): undefined reference to `InitFoo'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

jon: Which targets exactly are failing? Can you paste the full bazel command you used to reproduce?

maya: Failing targets: //core:static_lib, //apps/ingest:ingest_bin. I reproduced locally inside the new gcc13 image: `registry.redwood/toolchain:gcc13-2026-03-16`. Bazel command: `bazel build --config=linux_gcc13 //core:static_lib`. Rerun CI job once, same failure.

liam: Can you inspect the .a? `ar t` and `nm -C` to see if the object that should provide InitFoo is actually archived or if symbol got mangled/stripped.

maya: Ran the checks.
1234:~/repo$ ar t bazel-bin/core/libcore.a
foo.o
bar.o
utils.o

1234:~/repo$ nm -C bazel-bin/core/libcore.a | grep InitFoo || true
00000000 T InitFoo

So the member exists and symbol is present in the archive, but the linker still complains about undefined reference to `InitFoo`. Weird.

liam: Hmm. Two quick possibilities: 1) the archive is a thin archive (ar t shows members but linker can't resolve because objects are referenced externally), or 2) ar/binutils behavior changed and bazel's static linking step isn't including the member for some reason. Can you run `file bazel-bin/core/libcore.a` and `ar tv`?

maya: Output:
1234:~/repo$ file bazel-bin/core/libcore.a
bazel-bin/core/libcore.a: "current ar archive (thin)"

1234:~/repo$ ar tv bazel-bin/core/libcore.a
-rw-r--r-- 1 maya maya  1234 Mar 16 12:00 foo.o
-rw-r--r-- 1 maya maya  2345 Mar 16 12:00 bar.o
-rw-r--r-- 1 maya maya  345 Mar 16 12:00 utils.o

liam: There we go — it's a thin archive. We recently bumped binutils in the toolchain image and `ar` now defaults to producing thin archives in our build pipeline. Our linker invocation expects full archives (not thin). Thin archives reference external object files by path; if the final linker doesn't have access to those paths, you get undefined references even though `nm` shows symbols.

sre: Confirmed — nightly toolchain image roll included binutils 2.40 which changed default behavior for `ar` on our build scripts. Seeing similar failures in a different project.

jon: Short-term: can we force creation of full archives in the build by setting `ARFLAGS` or adding `-H`/`--format=gnu`? Bazel's C++ toolchain wrapper might need a flag. Also we could pin CI to previous toolchain image while we roll a fix.

maya: I pushed a quick patch to the CI job to pin `registry.redwood/toolchain:gcc12-stable` for the linux_gcc13 matrix entry and retriggered. Rerunning now.

CI-bot: rerun started (job 1234 pinned to gcc12-stable).

courtney: For the long-term, we should update our packaging step to pass `ar --format=gnu` or adjust bazel's `cc_toolchain` to force non-thin archives. I'll open a tracker and assign to eng-infra. Also want a postmortem note so product teams know why the roll caused breakage.

maya: Thanks — opening bug: https://issues.redwood.internal/RED-4123 "toolchain: ar defaults to thin archives -> linker failures". Adding notes and linking CI job.

liam: If anyone wants to bisect the exact binutils change, tag me and I'll take it, otherwise pinning + patch to force gnu format seems fine.

jon: Agree. Thanks for the quick triage, maya. Pinning + fix in the toolchain should unblock. :thumbsup:

maya: CI rerun with pinned image is green so I'm merging the temporary pin and will follow up on the toolchain fix.

courtney: adding follow-up tasks to our weekly infra sync.

maya: Closing out here — thanks folks. :tada:
